title: Specify metering heuristics for staggered cache aggregation
creator: Elena Morozova
description: Problem summary: We have recurring discrepancies between what customers expect to be billed and what the platform invoices for requests that benefit from prefix/KV caching and requests that are coalesced into larger batches. Observed symptoms include: (1) undercounting in quota dashboards for requests that hit the prefix cache across interleaved batches, (2) transient surge in billed tokens when a multi-request batch is split at the runtime and charged per-GPU without dedup accounting, and (3) rate-limit enforcement that consumes quota for coalesced prefetches even when subsequent requests hit KV cache. Goals: 1) Define a deterministic, auditable heuristic for token charging in presence of prefix/KV cache hits and batch coalescing. 2) Ensure quota and rate-limit counters reflect billable usage customers can predict. 3) Provide a migration and monitoring plan to catch regressions and communicate changes to customers.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Charging rule specified in RFC-style doc with clear pseudo-formulas for per-request charge when prefix cache hit, KV cache hit, or full decode

A2: Implementation plan and runtime hooks defined so that the accounting path receives annotated batch metadata (cache_hit_type, saved_tokens, batch_origin_id), and existing billing pipeline can use it

A3: Unit + integration tests that cover: single-request cache hit, multi-request coalesced batch with mixed hits, split-batch across GPUs, and prefetch-only requests (no user-visible tokens) to ensure they are not double-charged
A4: Backfilling telemetry to compare old vs new charge for a 48-hour window; discrepancies explained and <0.5% of invoices affected post-rollout
A5: Documentation updated for customers and quotas FAQ; release notes prepared
proposed_solution: High-level heuristic: - Bill generated tokens (model outputs) to the owning request always. - For prompt tokens: charge request.prompt_tokens - saved_by_prefix_cache - saved_by_kv_cache where saved_by_* comes from runtime counters attached to the request at batch construction time. saved_by_kv_cache is accounted per-request; if KV entries were reused across multiple requests in the same coalesced batch, attribute saved tokens only once per logical request (avoid deduping across distinct customer requests). For coalesced batches that run shared decoding on the same input prefix (e.g., identical warmup queries), detect 'shared_execution' and bill prompt tokens once to the originating request(s) per the policy: if the shared execution was triggered by prefetch/pipeline warmup (no customer-ID), mark as non-billable (but track cost internally). Implementation notes: add a lightweight BatchAccounting struct emitted by runtime when batching decisions are made, containing flat fields (batch_id, members:list_of_request_ids, per_request_saved_tokens:list_of_ints, shared_execution_flag). The billing pipeline will fold these signals into per-request billable token totals. Trade-offs: slightly more metadata emitted from runtime; but avoids complex post-hoc heuristics and reduces disputes.
rollout_plan: Step 1: RFC and design review (1 week) with billing, runtime, and product owners
Step 2: Add runtime instrumentation (feature-flag gated); emit accounting signals to debug stream only
Step 3: Implement billing consumer changes in safe mode (does not change invoices) and run side-by-side comparison for 7 days
Step 4: Automated test sweep + manual audit for top 50 customers by token volume
Step 5: Gradual opt-in rollout for new billing model (customers can opt in via flag), collect feedback
Step 6: Full rollout and deprecation of old heuristics after 30 days of opt-in telemetry stability
telemetry_changes: Emit per-request fields: runtime_saved_prefix_tokens, runtime_saved_kv_tokens, batch_origin_id, shared_execution_flag
Add daily diff dashboard comparing old_billed_tokens vs new_billed_tokens grouped by customer and model
Alert if >1% of requests see a delta > 100 tokens between old and new accounting during canary
Add a billing-audit endpoint to fetch detailed per-request accounting for dispute resolution
migration_notes: We will run the new accounting in observation mode for at least one billing cycle. During observation mode, both old and new billed totals will be recorded. After validation, we will switch invoices to the new model for future billing periods only; no retroactive charge adjustments will be applied except in exceptional cases documented by finance. Customer communications: a short FAQ and sample calculations for common patterns (single request with prefix hit, 10x batched inference with mixed hits, prefetch-only jobs).
test_plan: Unit tests for arithmetic of saved token subtraction and bounds checking (no negative charges)
Integration tests that simulate batching across multiple GPUs and assert per-request billed tokens match expectation
Load test that verifies emitted accounting metadata adds <3% latency to batch scheduling path at p95
E2E billing test that runs side-by-side consumer with historical traffic for 48 hours and compares invoice aggregates
